case_studies.modernization_thesis: Modernization became possible only after the system became understandable. The work restored reliable signal, mapped actual behavior, and created safer conditions for change across a shared Rails platform.
case_studies.distinctive_contribution: Mike's distinctive contribution was making system behavior explainable, connecting evidence to ownership, creating repeated learning practices, and protecting the prerequisites that made safer modernization possible.
case_studies.modernization_quote: “Fix what’s broken, upgrade the stuff that works, and stabilize the system to allow change. That is the real path to modernization.”
case_studies.quote_provenance: Mike's retrospective recollection, recorded November 20, 2025, referring to his OMF Tech ELT presentation. A May 15, 2025 record independently confirms the presentation and its substance.
case_studies.methodology_lesson: Innovation is repairing broken systems so they can be understood, improved, and moved forward. Mike's documented method is Inventory, Evaluate, Address. The modernization sequence is a later synthesis of what that work makes possible.

historical_method.name: Inventory → Evaluate → Address
historical_method.summary: This is Mike's IEA discovery sequence applied to the Acquisition domain in 2023: establish what exists, decide what is trustworthy and relevant, then take the smallest useful corrective action. Each new pass carries forward what was learned. The six-part modernization sequence is a broader synthesis across IEA, Panoramic View, and OpenTelemetry work.
historical_method.source_note: The documented initiative used a quotation attributed to Rear Admiral Grace Murray Hopper, “One accurate measurement is worth a thousand expert opinions.” The attribution belongs to that source record, not to Mike.

steps.name: Inventory
steps.action: Record feature flags, experiments, events, customer journeys, code assets, and the knowledge held by teams.
steps.gate: Can we describe what exists and where the evidence comes from?

steps.name: Evaluate
steps.action: Test relevance, viability, data quality, knowledge gaps, and the boundary of the Acquisition domain.
steps.gate: Do we know which signals and responsibilities can be trusted?

steps.name: Address
steps.action: Flatten unnecessary flags, end weak experiments, instrument systems, remove low-confidence events, and cross-train teams.
steps.gate: Did the intervention improve confidence without hiding the remaining uncertainty?

operating_model.name: Stabilize
operating_model.action: Restore reliable signal and contain the immediate operational risk.
operating_model.gate: Can the team make a bounded change without losing the ability to tell what happened?

operating_model.name: Understand
operating_model.action: Map customer journeys, dependencies, ownership, and actual runtime behavior.
operating_model.gate: Does the evidence connect the business path to code, data, infrastructure, and responsible teams?

operating_model.name: Improve
operating_model.action: Apply targeted fixes, standards, upgrades, and clearer workflows.

case_studies.title: Phalanx: Duel: Tabletop Rules to Multiplayer Engine
case_studies.summary: Designed a tactical card duel at Boy Scout Camp Tesomas in 2022 and prototyped its combat rules in Ruby. Rebuilt it as a server-authoritative TypeScript engine, with a deterministic engine package kept separate from the transport layer, a Go CLI, a TypeScript SDK, and an experimental SwiftUI client, now running live at phalanxduel.com.

dimensions.interaction_surface: WebSocket protocol (createMatch, joinMatch, watchMatch, action, authenticate) paired with an OpenAPI 3.0 REST surface for matchmaking, ladder, and replay, a TypeScript SDK, a Go CLI (duel-cli), and an experimental SwiftUI iOS client, all built against one shared schema contract.
dimensions.lateral_state_dependencies: 8-stage turn state machine (StartTurn through EndTurn) enforcing Target Chain, Boundary, and Carryover combat semantics, with Postgres storing match state, action history, and transaction logs as JSONB alongside Glicko-2 Elo snapshots tracked per ladder category.
dimensions.full_stack_topology: TypeScript monorepo separating a transport-only server from a deterministic, transport-free engine package, backed by Postgres via Drizzle, Docker-built deploys, Sentry error tracking, and an OTel Collector feeding OTel/LGTM observability across the server and Go client.
dimensions.supply_chain_exposure: AGPLv3 open-source codebase with 40+ operational wiki and docs guides, an independent combat verifier that checks 2,355,388 declared finite cases and pins a SHA-256 result digest, and CI-gated rule, replay, and playthrough verification ahead of every release.

outcomes: Built an explainable battle engine that records a versioned, step-by-step combat calculation for every attack, with named operands, ordered operators, and stable PD-RULE identifiers, driving live damage previews, narration, and spectator replay.
Verified the combat engine against an independent reference checker covering 2,355,388 declared finite cases, pinning a SHA-256 result digest as a bounded correctness proof.

Kept game state synchronized across WebSocket and REST paths for TypeScript, Go, and Swift clients, using role-specific projections and knowledge-safety tests that keep hidden hand and deck information out of what any client can see.

Shipped a live production platform (phalanxduel.com) with an automated release pipeline that builds an immutable GHCR container image, promotes it after health and readiness checks, and rolls back to the last known-good image on failure.

nodes.label: Aspect-Oriented Programming
nodes.description: A way to describe behavior that crosses many parts of a program, then apply it at selected boundaries.

nodes.label: pointcut
nodes.description: The rule that selects the places in a program where an aspect is allowed to run.

nodes.label: join point
nodes.description: A meaningful moment in execution, such as entering a method, leaving it, or handling an error.

nodes.label: advice
nodes.description: The behavior an aspect runs at a selected join point, often before, after, or when an error occurs.

nodes.label: instrumentation
nodes.description: Adding measurements or signals to a system so its behavior can be observed while it runs.

nodes.label: OpenTelemetry
nodes.description: An open standard and set of tools for producing traces, metrics, and logs that describe system behavior.

nodes.label: Strangler Fig pattern
nodes.description: An incremental migration approach that routes one capability at a time to a new system while the old system remains useful.

nodes.label: Conway's Law
nodes.description: The systems an organization builds tend to reflect the communication paths through which the organization works.

nodes.label: Reverse Conway Maneuver
nodes.description: Shaping team boundaries and communication paths so the system that emerges has the architecture the organization needs.

nodes.label: Golden Signals
nodes.description: Four useful starting measures for service health: latency, traffic, errors, and saturation.

nodes.label: service-level objective
nodes.description: A target for a measurable service outcome, including the boundary where the system is too hot or too cold.

nodes.label: System Cartography
nodes.description: A disciplined way to map a living system across code, runtime behavior, ownership, and organizational context before changing it.

nodes.label: AOP as the Bridge Between OpenTelemetry and the Strangler Fig
nodes.description: A field lesson on how Aspect-Oriented Programming makes cross-cutting behavior visible, supports OpenTelemetry, and helps teams find safer seams for incremental modernization.

nodes.label: AOP's Uses, Misuses, and Boundaries
nodes.description: When Aspect-Oriented Programming clarifies a system, when it hides control flow, and how to choose a boundary without creating invisible behavior.

nodes.label: From Fiverr to whisper.cpp: Building a Verifiable Oral History Pipeline
nodes.description: The long path from expensive, lossy outsourced transcription to a local, resumable, human-reviewed pipeline for preserving technical conversations.

nodes.label: A Simple Ruby Block as an AOP-Shaped Boundary
nodes.description: A small Ruby example showing how a block can make before, operation, exit, and error behavior explicit at a reusable boundary.

nodes.label: The Archive I Could Finally Build
nodes.description: What UGtastic, Dead Rabbit Radio, the Fluffle transcription experiment, Raspberry Pi processing, and local AI taught me about preserving oral history.

nodes.label: The Shortcut That Shifts Toward Knowledge
nodes.description: A small keyboard gesture as a reminder to slow down, orient, and move deliberately toward knowledge.

nodes.label: What Aspect-Oriented Programming Is
nodes.description: A plain-language introduction to aspects, join points, pointcuts, advice, and cross-cutting concerns, grounded in Mike Hall's PostSharp work.
